baseline_models.focus_anchor: The causative lostness in `yudlil`, the negated `wali min ba'dihi`, and the requested `mard` and `sabil` form one directional sequence.
baseline_models.mechanism: Departure from the intended course removes both adjacency and delegated care; only after that support topology has collapsed does a route of return become the wrongdoers' explicit object.

activation_trace.role: Deviation from guidance supplies the initiating displacement from an intended course.
Nearness without an interval makes the negated wali the missing adjacent link.
Taking charge of an affair makes the missing link an absent custodian, not merely a sympathetic friend.
Afterness and succession place any imagined replacement on the far side of God's act.
Return to a prior place or state supplies the desired reversal.
An extended traversable road turns the wish to return into a demand for an executable route.

changed_reading.before: A person whom God leads astray has no helper, and the punished ask to go back.
changed_reading.after: Divine displacement leaves no adjacent successor or custodian through whom return could be operationalized; the late plea therefore asks for a route after the relational route itself has vanished.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The verse frames the wrongdoers with `wa-tara`, repeats sight in `ra'awu al-'adhab`, and only then gives them speech.
baseline_models.mechanism: The addressee's encompassing sight precedes the wrongdoers' event-bound sight. Their perception becomes adequate only when punishment is present, so utterance is generated by belated exposure rather than deliberation.

activation_trace.role: Eye or insight joins the outer observer's seeing to the wrongdoers' own eventual perception.
Causing something to appear sharpens the scene from neutral observation into forced disclosure.
Painful punishment is the object whose arrival finally makes their seeing consequential.
Articulated speech is the delayed output produced once sight can no longer avoid its object.

changed_reading.before: The verse reports that the wrongdoers see punishment and ask a question.
changed_reading.after: The verse stages an asymmetry of vision: they are already visible to the addressee, but they themselves truly see only at impact, when sight involuntarily turns into a plea.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: `Al-zalimin` stands between the double seeing and their request for a `mard` by a `sabil`.
baseline_models.mechanism: The branch image of wrongdoing as putting or sending something outside its proper time or place is reversed onto its agents: those who produced displacement seek to be placed back, but only after the temporal boundary has passed.

activation_trace.role: Putting a thing outside its proper time or place gives wrongdoing a concrete displacement mechanism.
Withholding a right adds blocked delivery to the agents' prior conduct.
Afterness supplies the passed boundary that makes attempted replacement belated.
Restoration to a former place or state reverses the wrongdoers' own displacement pattern.
A traversable means would be required to make that restoration real.

changed_reading.after: Agents characterized by mistiming, misplacement, and withholding now seek their own re-placement into the former order, but they ask only after the relevant boundary.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah repeatedly distinguishes adopted guardians from the one wali who guards, revives, and relieves. Its near-verbatim restatement after the focus removes `wali` and leaves only the negated `sabil`, making `min ba'dihi` a failed succession structure.

activation_trace.role: Custodial charge anchors the focus negation in an office of effective care.
Adopted awliya supply attempted alternative custodianship.
Guarding and preserving assign effective oversight to God.
The one who sufficiently manages an affair clarifies the role explicitly denied to the messenger here.
Relief of one in distress makes guardianship materially effective after despair.
Tender mercy is what the wali spreads rather than merely a title he bears.
Protective alliance identifies the agent of post-despair relief as the wali.
The plural absence of custodians immediately after the focus generalizes its singular negation.
The repeated causative deviation reopens the focus condition almost verbatim.
The restatement contracts missing guardian and missing traversable route into the same outcome.

structural_cues: 42:6 distinguishes adopted awliya from God's guarding while denying the messenger a wakil role.
42:9 names God the wali; 42:28 couples that title with relief after despair; 42:31 and 42:46 deny alternate wali, nasir, or sabil.
42:46 repeats the focus's `wa-man yudlil Allah` formula but replaces `wali min ba'dihi` with the direct result `no sabil`.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the recurring guardian contrasts and the 42:46 compression; I infer that `min ba'dihi` marks an impossible replacement or succession, while the live alternative is the simpler temporal sense 'after God's abandonment.'

changed_reading.before: No helper can rescue the person after God leads him astray.
changed_reading.after: The surah has already tested substitute guardians and assigned effective preservation and relief to God alone; once that wali relation is lost, no office can be transferred and no route remains.

context_deltas.mechanism: Immediately before the focus, `sabil` is first denied against the vindicated and then asserted against those who wrong and transgress. In the focus, the same route-word changes direction from `against` the wrongdoers to the wrongdoers' desired route `toward` return.

activation_trace.role: Return supplies the destination toward which the wrongdoers try to redirect the route.
A traversable road carries the grammatical reversal from prosecutorial access to desired escape.
No road `against` the vindicated establishes the protected side of the legal topology.
The road asserted `against` wrongdoers becomes the operative avenue of liability.
Withholding people from their rights identifies those against whom the avenue lies.
Transgressing the limit supplies the actionable excess that activates the avenue.
A binding entitlement fixes the limit that their transgression violates.
Punitive pain is the stated terminus of the avenue that the focus then shows.

structural_cues: The consecutive constructions move from 42:41 `ma 'alayhim min sabil`, through 42:42 `innama al-sabil 'ala`, to 42:44 `hal ila mardin min sabil`.
The focus repeats both `al-zalimin` and `al-'adhab` from 42:42 after the directional use of `sabil` has been established.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated noun, adjacent sequence, and the prepositional switch from `ala` to `ila`; I infer one route changing legal direction, while the live alternative is ordinary polysemy between a ground of complaint and a path of escape.

changed_reading.before: The wrongdoers ask whether any escape route exists.
changed_reading.after: They ask to appropriate as an escape route the very `sabil` that the preceding legal sequence has laid against them; the grammar turns the avenue of liability around, but only in their speech.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus's speech occurs when punishment is seen; the next ayah commands a response before a day whose return, refuge, and denial are all negated. Return is therefore blocked by sequence, not merely distance.

activation_trace.role: Sight marks the late event at which the wrongdoers finally formulate their request.
Return names the reversal they seek only after seeing.
Answering speech supplies the timely response demanded before the terminal event.
Temporal precedence establishes that response must occur in advance.
The explicit no-return day resolves the focus's interrogative request.
Seeking protection in a refuge is separately closed, preventing `mard` from being recast as shelter.
The opposite of recognition supplies the final denied maneuver: disavowing what has become visible.

structural_cues: 42:44 orders seeing punishment before asking; 42:47 orders responding to the Lord before the no-return day arrives.
The next occurrence of `mard` is declarative and negated, answering the focus's interrogative `hal`.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the before/after imperatives and repeated `mard`; I infer that the plea fails because it is speech outside the response window, while the alternative is that 42:47 only describes the day independently of their missed response.

changed_reading.before: Their request is denied because return from punishment is impossible.
changed_reading.after: Their words have the form of response but arrive in the wrong temporal slot: seeing produces an answer only after the commanded pre-event response window has closed.

context_deltas.mechanism: A three-stage visual sequence surrounds the focus: the wrongdoers are seen fearing what they earned, they see punishment and speak, then they are displayed while looking only from a concealed edge of vision. Sight moves from apprehension to forced recognition to public exposure.

activation_trace.role: Mutual facing under visibility joins the outer `you see` frame to their inner seeing.
The first `you see` makes them observable before the focus event.
Care mixed with fear supplies anticipatory apprehension.
What they acquired ties the approaching object to their own activity.
A severe descending event converts anticipation into impending impact.
Making visible resumes the outer frame after their plea.
Presentation for inspection turns punishment into a public display.
Lowered submission supplies their displayed bodily posture.
Breakage under domination explains why their field of vision contracts.
Directed looking persists even when full visual agency is lost.
The edge or limit of a thing reduces their look to a visual margin.
Concealment qualifies the marginal glance as an attempted retreat inside unavoidable display.

structural_cues: 42:22, 42:44, and 42:45 each open or pivot with `tara`, producing a distributed visual frame.
The focus alone doubles the seeing root, while 42:45 follows with display, lowered posture, and a hidden side-glance.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated vision, earned event, display, and contracted glance; I infer an exposure apparatus that progressively removes visual control, while the alternative is a straightforward chronological description with no special visual mechanism.

changed_reading.before: An observer sees the wrongdoers react when they see punishment.
changed_reading.after: They pass through a controlled economy of visibility: seen while fearing, forced to see at impact, then made fully visible while permitted only a concealed peripheral look.

context_deltas.mechanism: Earlier, dispute about the Hour is named distant lostness. At the close, revelation becomes light that guides to a straight path, the path of God, toward whom affairs become. The focus's missing `sabil` is thus the negative image of a revealed directional corridor available before sight of punishment.

activation_trace.role: Departure from guidance anchors the focus in a path regime.
The requested traversable route is the missing negative counterpart to the closing path.
Doubt and hesitation supply the cognitive motion that precedes distant lostness.
Explicit deviation about the Hour anticipates the focus condition.
Distance turns that deviation into remoteness from recovery.
Illumination supplies visibility before punishment rather than visibility caused by it.
Gentle direction to the road supplies the available opposite of causative lostness.
The straight path gives positive shape to the route absent in the focus.
Straightness, balance, and uprightness define the path's maintained alignment.
Naming it God's path identifies the corridor's destination and ownership.
Becoming toward an outcome supplies the surah's final directional return.

structural_cues: 42:18 joins dispute over the Hour to `dalal ba'id`; 42:44 joins causative lostness to a missing `sabil` of return.
42:52-53 close with light, doubled guidance, a straight path, God's path, and all affairs moving toward God.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the lostness-distance cluster and the light-guidance-path closure; I infer that the focus asks too late for the corridor previously offered, while the live alternatives are that `sabil` and `sirat` need not form one system and the final movement of affairs is not voluntary return.

changed_reading.before: The condemned ask for any way back after judgment.
changed_reading.after: Their absent route is the negative silhouette of the surah's revealed light-path: seeing at punishment cannot substitute for the earlier illumination by which a person is guided onto the corridor.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the water-sweetness and withholding branches around lexical `adhab`, not its ordinary punishment branch alone. It remains anchored in the focus's `adhab` and missing `wali`, and 42:28 puts rain, revived spread, mercy, and wali together after despair. Downstream prose should present it as a material counter-image of deprivation, not as an etymological replacement for punishment.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus combines `al-'adhab` with the absence of a later wali; both roots carry packet branches involving sweetness or withholding and subsequent rain.

activation_trace.role: Punitive pain preserves the surface reading that contains the outlier.
Sweet, potable water supplies the positive substance whose loss can be felt as deprivation.
Withholding and weaning provide the functional arrow from punishment to denied relief.
Rain that succeeds earlier rain makes `no wali after Him` imagistically a failure of any subsequent shower.
Cut-off hope supplies the dry terminal state from which relief normally arrives.
Life-giving rain supplies the material opposite of terminal withholding.
Rain reviving dry herbage turns mercy into restored spread and life.
Tender mercy names the relief being spread after despair.
The wali as a following rain links guardianship to renewed provision after barrenness.

changed_reading.before: Punishment is an externally inflicted pain from which no protector rescues them.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, punishment also appears as irreversible weaning from the sweet, life-restoring relief that the wali spreads after despair: this time no later rain follows.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it uses the packet's non-dominant `m r d` mapping of `mard`, especially the pole that pushes a vessel, and lets 42:32-35 activate it. It remains anchored in the exact focus form and its paired `sabil`, but the mapping is form-distant. Downstream prose should render it only as a whole-surah material analogy, never as the lexical translation of `mard`.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus form `mard` resolves both to ordinary return and to a split `m r d` inventory containing the implement by which a boat is pushed.

activation_trace.role: Pushing a vessel with a pole supplies a concrete maneuvering image inside the split mapping of `mard`.
A traversable course turns the requested return into a search for steerage.
Flowing motion supplies the ships' normal capacity to traverse.
The broad body of water supplies the material field for the maneuver.
Loss of motion removes the ships' ordinary means of progress.
Wind and moving air name the withdrawn agency that normally drives them.
Stillness after movement fixes the vessels in a becalmed state.
Being brought into destruction makes failed maneuver terminal rather than inconvenient.
Turning aside from a direction supplies the escape maneuver explicitly denied to disputants.

changed_reading.before: The wrongdoers ask abstractly for a way to return.
changed_reading.after: As a contained material analogy, they resemble passengers on a becalmed, doomed vessel asking whether any pole, course, or lateral maneuver can still turn them back after the driving wind has been withdrawn.

strongest_changes: The adjacent 42:41-44 sequence reverses `sabil` from an avenue lying against wrongdoers into the route they wish could lead toward return.
42:47 converts the focus's question into a missed response window: answer before the no-return day, not after punishment becomes visible.
The repeated guardian passages and 42:46 compression make `wali min ba'dihi` an impossible transfer of effective custody, not only the absence of generic help.
The 42:22, 42:44, and 42:45 visual sequence changes seeing into progressive public exposure and loss of visual agency.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah context exposed a directional architecture that the focus alone only hints at: legal `sabil` immediately before it, no-return immediately after it, and a closing light-guidance-path corridor. The split `mard` inventory also preserved a vessel analogy activated by the earlier becalmed ships.
remaining_uncertainties: `Min ba'dihi` may indicate simple temporal aftermath rather than succession into a vacated guardian role.
The sweetness, withholding, and following-rain activation around `adhab` and `wali` is materially coherent but remains associative rather than a replacement lexical sense.
The vessel reading depends on the non-dominant `m r d` mapping and must remain an analogy, not a translation.
The closing `sirat` and the focus's `sabil` may be parallel directional terms without constituting one technical corridor.
